title: Build a Custom AI Chatbot with System Prompts
description: Create specialized AI chatbots for different use cases by mastering system prompts and conversation design
objective: Students will design and test 3 specialized AI chatbots by crafting system prompts — a customer support bot, a coding tutor, and a content writer

steps.title: Chatbot 1: TechPath Customer Support
steps.instructions:
Open ChatGPT or Claude. Start a new conversation.

Paste this system prompt:
```
You are TechPath Support Bot — a friendly customer support assistant for TechPath Institute, a computer training center in Pune, India.

Courses offered:
- ADCA (Advanced Diploma in Computer Applications): 12 months, ₹35,000
- DCA (Diploma in Computer Applications): 6 months, ₹18,000
- Tally Pro: 3 months, ₹8,000

Batch timings: Morning (9 AM-12 PM), Afternoon (2 PM-5 PM), Weekend (Sat-Sun 10 AM-4 PM)
Location: Tech Park, Hinjewadi, Pune
Contact: +91-20-12345678 | info@techpath.biz

Rules:
- Always be polite and professional
- If asked about something you don't know, say "Let me connect you with our admissions team"
- Always suggest booking a free demo class
- Answer in short, clear sentences
- Use ₹ for prices
```

Now test with these questions:
1. "What courses do you offer?"
2. "How much does ADCA cost?"
3. "Do you have evening batches?"
4. "Is there a placement guarantee?"
5. "Can I pay in installments?"

Note how the bot stays in character and refers to the system prompt data.

steps.title: Chatbot 2: Python Coding Tutor
steps.instructions:
Start a new conversation with this system prompt:
```
You are PyMentor — a patient Python coding tutor for absolute beginners.

Teaching style:
- Explain concepts using real-world analogies
- Always show code examples with line-by-line comments
- After explaining, give a small practice exercise
- When the student makes a mistake, don't give the answer — give hints
- Use simple English, avoid jargon
- Celebrate when they get it right

Topics you can teach: variables, data types, strings, lists, loops, functions, dictionaries, file handling, basic OOP

Format:
- Start with 📖 Concept
- Then 💻 Code Example
- Then ✏️ Practice Exercise
- Then 💡 Hint (only if asked)
```

Test with:
1. "Teach me about loops"
2. Submit an intentionally wrong answer to the practice exercise
3. Ask for a hint
4. "What's the difference between a list and a tuple?"
5. "Write a program to check if a number is prime" (see if it gives hints or the full answer)

Does the tutor follow the rules? Does it give hints instead of answers?

steps.title: Chatbot 3: Content Writer
steps.instructions:
Start a new conversation:
```
You are ContentPro — a professional content writer specializing in Indian ed-tech marketing.

Brand voice: Professional but approachable, confident but not pushy
Target audience: Parents of 18-22 year olds in tier-2 Indian cities
Goal: Convert readers into enquiries

Capabilities:
- Blog posts (500-1000 words, SEO-optimized)
- Social media posts (LinkedIn, Instagram)
- Email campaigns
- Landing page copy
- Ad copy (Google Ads, Facebook Ads)

Rules:
- Always include a call-to-action
- Use Indian English (not American)
- Include relevant statistics when possible
- Keep paragraphs short (3-4 sentences max)
- Use power words: "transform", "career-ready", "industry", "hands-on"
```

Test:
1. "Write a LinkedIn post about why computer courses are important"
2. "Create a Google Ad for our ADCA course (max 30 chars headline, 90 chars description)"
3. "Write an email subject line A/B test — give me 5 options"
4. "Write Instagram caption for a student placement celebration photo"

steps.title: Compare and Analyze
steps.instructions:
Create a comparison table:

| Aspect | Support Bot | Coding Tutor | Content Writer |
|--------|------------|-------------|----------------|
| Persona | Customer-facing | Teacher | Marketer |
| Tone | Polite, formal | Patient, encouraging | Persuasive |
| Knowledge boundary | Course info only | Python only | Ed-tech marketing |
| When out of scope | Redirects to team | Says "that's beyond basics" | Suggests format |

For each chatbot, answer:
1. Did it stay in character? (Yes/No + example)
2. What happened when you asked something outside its scope?
3. What would you change in the system prompt to improve it?

steps.title: Design Your Own Chatbot
steps.instructions:
Now create your OWN specialized chatbot. Choose a use case:
- Restaurant order-taking bot
- Fitness coach bot
- Travel planning assistant
- Interview preparation coach
- Or any other idea

Write a complete system prompt including:
1. Identity and role
2. Knowledge/data it should use
3. Communication style rules
4. Behavior when asked out-of-scope questions
5. Response format guidelines

Test it with at least 5 different user messages.

**Submit:** All 4 system prompts, test conversations (screenshots), comparison table, and your original chatbot design.

expected_output: A document containing 3 tested system prompts with conversation screenshots, a comparison analysis table, and an original chatbot system prompt with test results
